## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dīpaṅkarabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 3) is a section of the *Buddhavaṁsa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. It relates the account of Dīpaṅkara, the first of the twenty-four buddhas preceding Gotama, and marks the starting point of Gotama's path to buddhahood [Gaffney 2003]. Being the longest chapter of the *Buddhavaṁsa*, it recounts Gotama Buddha's recollections of his past existence as the ascetic Sumedha and his initial resolution to follow the bodhisatta path, introducing concepts novel to the text, notably the full formulation of the ten perfections (*pāramī*s) [Gaffney 2003]. The text employs formulaic, chant-like enumerations of epithets and qualities [Collins 1998], and uses the canonical term *khaṇa* in the sense of an auspicious moment or spiritual opportunity [von Rospatt 1995].

The text served as a foundational source for later biographical and narrative literature: it is preserved almost in its entirety within the *Nidānakathā* of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [Buddhist Forum 1996]. DharmaNexus confirms extensive text reuse across early Pali commentaries, sharing extensive passages with the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* (segments 1.1–31.4), the *Buddhavaṁsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* (segments 1.1–18.4), and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (segments 1.1–18.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns recurring stock formulas between this text and subsequent *Buddhavaṁsa* biographies (such as Bv 21, Bv 12, and Bv 9), while identifying cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032) and the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu Avadāna* [DharmaNexus].
